content_sections.heading: About Chamarajanagar Anganwadi Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: The recruitment fills vacant posts at Anganwadi centres run by the Women and Child Development Department in Chamarajanagar district, Karnataka. The Deputy Commissioner's office has asked the National Informatics Centre (NIC), Chamarajanagar, to invite the applications online. Selection follows the Karnataka Government guidelines in Government Order No. ಮಮಇ 154 ಐಸಿಡಿ 2020 dated 03-12-2022 and its modification order dated 18-11-2024, both attached to the notice.

content_sections.heading: Chamarajanagar Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 Important Dates
content_sections.text: The documents are attached to the online application itself, so 4 December 2026 is the single deadline for both the form and the documents.

content_sections.heading: Vacancies by Project / Block
content_sections.text: Most of the posts, 271 of 390, are Anganwadi Helper posts. The vacancies are spread over the 5 taluk Child Development Projects of the district. The notice does not give a project-wise or centre-wise list.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: Only women and transgender minority women are eligible to apply for the Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Applicants for both posts must be within the age limit of 19-35 years. Persons with disabilities get an age relaxation of 10 years. The notice does not print a cut-off date for counting age. For an Anganwadi centre in a rural area, the applicant must live in that revenue village. For an Anganwadi centre in an urban area, the applicant must live in that revenue ward and must have a residence certificate from the competent authority. Election wards are not considered. Residence is confirmed by a three-year residence certificate from the Tahsildar or Deputy Tahsildar, supported by an Aadhaar card, ration card or voter identity card. Applicants from a local majire, tanda or hadi must get the relevant residence certificate from the competent authority. In Anganwadi centres in areas where the minority community makes up 25 per cent of the population, applicants who know that community's language along with Kannada are selected. Preference for Anganwadi Worker: candidates holding an ECCE diploma course from D.S.E.R.T., JOC course or N.T.T. course from Government-recognised institutions, a Diploma in Nutrition, a Home Science certificate course, or one-year nursery or pre-primary training certificate related to Anganwadi activities get first preference and +5 bonus marks. Further rules for Anganwadi Helper: Candidates who passed S.S.L.C. from schools or open schools under the Karnataka Secondary Education Examination Board must have studied Kannada as first or second language and general mathematics and social science; they are considered if the certificate or marks card shows maximum 625 and minimum 219 marks. For candidates who studied in other states with Kannada as first or second language, if the maximum and minimum SSLC marks fixed in that state differ from those fixed in Karnataka, only candidates who studied in Karnataka are considered. Whatever the medium or state of study, Anganwadi Helpers must have studied Kannada as first or second language. For candidates whose mother tongue is not Kannada, the selection committee may hold an interview and, if needed, test reading and writing in Kannada before deciding. Candidates should check the official notification for the full eligibility rules of each post.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection for both posts is on merit: a combined list is prepared online on the total of the marks in the prescribed qualification and the bonus marks. The notice describes no written examination. When widows apply, they are selected directly at third priority, after acid attack survivors and residents of department institutions, without considering the other applications. A woman who becomes a widow after applying is not considered. Among widows, the widow of a farmer who died by suicide gets first priority. The place where the widow currently lives, as shown in her residence certificate, is taken as her residence. If two widows apply for one post, the one with the higher marks may be selected. Widows must attach the husband's death certificate or the widow certificate. The notice fixes the extent of physical disability as not more than 40 per cent. The place shown in the residence certificate is taken as the candidate's residence. If there is doubt about the extent of disability, the candidate is asked to appear in person before the selection committee, which decides whether she can do the job. The taluk-level verification committee, headed by the Tahsildar, checks the applications and sends the list to the Deputy Director. The district selection committee, chaired by the Deputy Commissioner, meets within 7 working days after the last date. Applications without any required document are rejected; unclear or incomplete documents are not considered. Candidates with the highest marks are selected and a provisional selection list is published on the notice board the same day. Seven days are given for objections; the final selection list is published on the notice board after they are considered. If more than one candidate has equal marks, the older candidate is preferred; if the age is also equal, a widow or divorced woman is preferred. The decision of the selection committee is final.

faq.question: Q1. How many vacancies are there in Chamarajanagar Anganwadi Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are 390 vacancies: 119 Anganwadi Worker and 271 Anganwadi Helper posts in the 5 taluk Child Development Projects of Chamarajanagar district.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: Online applications open on 5 November 2026 and the last date is 4 December 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for the Anganwadi Worker post?
faq.answer: The Anganwadi Worker must have passed at least P.U.C. and studied Kannada as first or second language in S.S.L.C.; ECCE, JOC, NTT, nutrition, home science or nursery training gives first preference and +5 bonus marks.

faq.question: Q4. What is the qualification for the Anganwadi Helper post?
faq.answer: The Anganwadi Helper must have passed at least SSLC or equivalent and studied Kannada as first or second language.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: The age limit for both posts is 19-35 years, with a 10-year relaxation for persons with disabilities.

faq.question: Q6. Who can apply?
faq.answer: Only women and transgender minority women who live in the revenue village (rural centre) or revenue ward (urban centre) of the Anganwadi centre can apply.

faq.question: Q7. How are candidates selected?
faq.answer: A merit list is prepared on the marks in the prescribed qualification plus bonus marks; a provisional list is published, 7 days are given for objections, and then the final list is published on the notice board.

faq.question: Q8. Who gets bonus marks?
faq.answer: Acid attack survivors, persons with disabilities, daughters of ex-Devadasis, project displaced persons and divorced women get +5 marks, and residents of department institutions with at least 3 years' stay get +10 marks.

faq.question: Q9. Is the Anganwadi post a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. The notice states the Anganwadi Worker / Helper post is entirely honorary service and not a permanent post.

faq.question: Q10. Are documents uploaded with the online form?
faq.answer: Yes. The required documents, attested by a gazetted officer, must be attached to the online application, and applications missing any required document are rejected.
